title: Compressibility, Turbulence and High Speed Flow
label: Start here
description: The backbone of this reading path: governing equations, density-weighted variables, and prediction strategies.
scope: Read Chapters 2 and 3 for the equations, then Chapter 5 for DNS, LES, and RANS. Derive the terms before comparing closure models. The second edition was released in 2013; the shop also lists a later product date.

title: Large Eddy Simulation for Compressible Flows
authors: Eric Garnier · Nikolaus Adams · Pierre Sagaut
label: Filtering & LES
description: Connect the filtered equations to subgrid modeling, numerical discretization, and practical compressible LES.
scope: Begin with the LES governing equations, then follow the relationship between the subgrid model and numerical discretization. Keep explicit filtering, implicit filtering, and numerical dissipation distinct.

title: Compressibility Effects on Turbulence
label: Field overview
description: A foundational review for organizing the physical effects that sit under the word compressibility.
scope: Read as a historical map, then pair it with current DNS and scaling papers. Mean-property variation, pressure-driven dilatation, and shock interactions are different questions.

title: Mean velocity scaling for compressible wall turbulence with heat transfer
label: Scaling · foundation
description: A reference point for following later work on velocity transformations with variable density and viscosity.
scope: A foundational comparison, not a claim about the latest state of the art. Record the thermal condition and geometry before comparing transformed profiles; a mean-profile collapse does not establish agreement in every statistic.

title: Velocity transformation for compressible wall-bounded turbulent flows with and without heat transfer
authors: Kevin P. Griffin · Lin Fu · Parviz Moin
label: Scaling · mean velocity
description: A total-stress-based transformation to read alongside Trettel–Larsson and more recent scaling proposals.
scope: Compare the tested flow families and assumptions as well as the transformed curves. Keep dimensional quantities, normalization choices, and the limits of equilibrium assumptions visible.

title: A composite mean temperature transformation for compressible turbulent boundary layers
label: Scaling · temperature
description: A recent temperature-scaling paper using a composite transformation for adiabatic and isothermal walls.
scope: Compare the DNS validation cases and wall conditions with the velocity-transformation literature. Mean temperature and mean velocity transformations address related but different observables.

title: Near-wall model for compressible turbulent boundary layers based on an inverse velocity transformation
authors: Kevin P. Griffin · Lin Fu · Parviz Moin
label: Scaling → wall modeling
description: A bridge from compressibility transformations to a practical near-wall modeling formulation.
scope: Follow the inverse transformation and its assumptions before treating it as a LES closure. Distinguish an a-priori profile comparison from an a-posteriori simulation assessment.

title: Turbulence Modeling in the Age of Data
authors: Karthik Duraisamy · Gianluca Iaccarino · Heng Xiao
label: Where can ML help?
description: Frame data-driven modeling around model uncertainty, physical constraints, and what training data can actually identify.
scope: A general turbulence-modeling review, not a hypersonic ML validation. Use it to formulate questions about closure discovery, uncertainty, and transfer across flow regimes.

title: Machine Learning for Fluid Mechanics
authors: Steven L. Brunton · Bernd R. Noack · Petros Koumoutsakos
label: Where can ML help?
description: A wider map of opportunities in model reduction, inference, control, and scientific data analysis.
scope: Start with the scientific question and a physical baseline. For HCT, test generalization across Mach number, Reynolds number, thermal conditions, and geometry rather than relying on a random snapshot split.

title: Machine-learning wall model of large-eddy simulation for low- and high-speed flows over rough surfaces
label: ML · wall-modeled LES
description: A recent example of applying learned wall modeling to both low- and high-speed flow cases.
scope: Preprint status is explicit. Read its a-posteriori tests and the training/test conditions; high-speed coverage should not be read as validation for every hypersonic or high-enthalpy regime.

title: Compressible boundary-layer DNS profiles
venue: University of Maryland · data and case inputs
label: Reproduce a profile
description: A directly usable starting point: averaged profiles and input files for eight compressible boundary-layer cases.
scope: The source covers Mach 2–10 and cold, adiabatic, and heated walls with a calorically perfect gas. These are averaged profiles, not full instantaneous fields. Cite Kumar and Larsson (PRF 2025) as requested by the data page; check its README and normalization.

title: NASA supersonic & hypersonic flat-plate DNS
authors: Chao Zhang · Lian Duan · Meelan M. Choudhari
venue: NASA TMR · companion AIAA Journal study
label: Validate wall statistics
description: Download high-speed flat-plate statistics and turbulent kinetic energy budgets from the relocated Turbulence Modeling Resource.
scope: The source spans nominal freestream Mach 2.5–14 and wall-to-recovery temperature ratios 0.18–1.0, with no high-enthalpy effects included. These are statistics and budget files, not raw three-dimensional snapshots. Each file begins with detailed README information. Companion paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7802740/

title: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database
label: Build an analysis baseline
description: Practice reproducible sampling, statistics, and data-access workflows on well-documented turbulence datasets.
scope: An adjacent resource: many canonical datasets are incompressible. Check the individual dataset, resolution, access terms, and sampling strategy; do not label it hypersonic validation data.

title: Wall Modeled Large Eddy Simulation of High-Enthalpy Hypersonic Flows
authors: Ryan L. MacDonald · NASA research program
label: High-enthalpy modeling
description: See how wall modeling connects to high-temperature physics and high-enthalpy hypersonic applications.
scope: A research project description, not a completed validation result. Use it to understand the modeling questions; seek the resulting papers for evidence of performance.

title: Simulations Provide Insight into Shock Wave/Boundary-Layer Interactions
authors: Manan Vyas · Datta Gaitonde · NASA and Ohio State
label: Shock interactions
description: An application-facing view of wall-resolved LES, shock interactions, and comparison with experiments.
scope: An older but useful application example. Keep the actual configuration and Mach regime explicit before transferring conclusions to hypersonic vehicle prediction.

title: Second-mode Waves in Hypersonic Transition: Energy Balance, Kinematics and Mechanics
authors: NASA Advanced Modeling & Simulation seminar series
label: Transition & thermal effects
description: A current aerospace perspective on hypersonic boundary-layer transition and thermal effects.
scope: Transition and fully developed turbulence are distinct problems. Follow the cited studies and reference conditions; a seminar page is an entry point, not a substitute for the underlying evidence.

title: RANS vs. LES: averaging, filtering, and the density-weighted equations
label: Work through the math
description: Start from continuity and momentum, define the operators, and see exactly where the unclosed stress appears.
scope: A sourced study note on the continuous equations, with commutation assumptions stated explicitly. It does not derive a full energy closure or claim a new turbulence model.
